thread:
Noah: Quick heads-up
I've been debugging the Go generator sampleapp and hit a surprising UX footgun: when a caller cancels the ctx during the generator handshake and immediately retries, the app can either hang (Result() blocks) or observe duplicated partial tokens. This hits small services that do tight cancel/retry loops. Anyone else seen this?

Zara: Yep, we've seen both behaviors in internal reports. Two separate root causes: (A) if internal handshake goroutine is blocked (auth refresh/TLS probe) Result() can block because EOF never arrives; (B) if transport/socket buffers get into an odd state a retry can replay fragments.

Ian: Can you paste a tiny repro snippet?

Noah: Minimal pattern I used:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 150*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
iter, err := gen.Generate(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return "", err }
for tok := range iter.Stream() { out += tok }
// this can block if ctx canceled during handshake
return iter.Result(), nil
```

Zara: Thanks. Two quick mitigation patterns we recommend in docs: (1) generator-per-retry: construct a fresh Generator/transport for each retry (safe but higher cost); (2) drain-and-close: spawn a goroutine to consume Stream() and call iter.Close(ctx) (we have a helper in a fork) when ctx.Done().

Ian: From an SDK perspective we discussed adding a couple of changes: - Iterator.Close(ctx) to force cleanup - ResultWithContext(ctx) so callers can avoid indefinite blocking - Transport option ResetOnRetry to tear down fd and clear buffers between attempts - RetryPolicy to let users choose fresh-transport vs reuse

Noah: I prototyped a safe client-side pattern that is small and easy to add to quickstart. Example:
```go
func safeConsume(ctx context.Context, iter sdk.Iterator) (string, error) {
  tokCh := make(chan string)
  done := make(chan struct{})
  go func() {
    for t := range iter.Stream() { tokCh <- t }
    close(done)
  }()
  var out string
  for {
    select {
    case <-ctx.Done():
      // force cleanup and return early
      iter.Close(context.Background())
      return "", ctx.Err()
    case t := <-tokCh:
      out += t
    case <-done:
      return iter.Result(), nil
    }
  }
}
```

Zara: That sample looks good for quickstart. We should land a similar snippet and mention generator-per-retry tradeoffs. Also call out auth-refresh races: prefer rotating tokens at transport layer (not per-request) to avoid mid-handshake 401->reauth races.

Ian: On the API side I opened a small PR that implements Iterator.Close(ctx) and adds ResultWithContext(ctx) as an opt-in. We'll keep the old Result() but mark it with a doc note. Also added a simple Transport.WithResetOnRetry(true) prototype.

DocsBot: Issue created: #5190 "go-sdk: streaming UX - Close/ResultWithContext + transport reset on retry"

Noah: Great. I also added a short e2e that fuzzes cancels mid-handshake and a tiny sample app showing the safeConsume pattern + generator-per-retry comparison (latency numbers included). PR is up.

CI-bot: PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/270 (ci: linux/amd64 pass, darwin flake)

Zara: Nice. Let's land the SDK changes first (iterator.Close + ResultWithContext) then follow up with quickstart and migration notes. We'll also update streaming FAQ and add a "when to recreate Generator" section.

Ian: Agreed. I added unit tests that simulate a mid-handshake 401 and ensure Close(ctx) unblocks. I also left comments on perf tradeoffs for ResetOnRetry.

Noah: Thanks all 389680 I'll update the onboarding quickstart PR after the SDK PR merges and add a CHANGES entry calling out the new safer patterns. Closing this thread when PR merges.
